references.text: Jacob bought a portion of the field at Shechem from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father. This shows Jacob's early connection to the Shechem area and his claim to this land.

Simeon and Levi attacked Shechem with the sword and plundered the city after the incident involving Dinah. This is the likely background for Jacob's statement about having taken Shechem 'with my sword and my bow' from the Amorites.

Joseph's bones, which the Israelites had brought with them from Egypt, were buried in Shechem on the piece of land that Jacob had bought. This shows the fulfillment of Jacob's gift of Shechem to Joseph.
Joseph's sons (Ephraim and Manasseh) received their inheritance in the promised land, as a fulfillment of Jacob's promise of an extra portion for Joseph beyond his brothers.
The birthright was given to Joseph's sons, and Judah became the strongest tribe. This explains why Jacob gave Joseph an extra inheritance ('one portion more than your brothers').
Jesus came to Sychar in Samaria, near the piece of land that Jacob gave to his son Joseph. This is a direct New Testament reference to Gen 48:22.
